raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On gfx950 with AITER enabled, the uncompressed sparse indexer of DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x (`index_topk` 2048) now takes AITER's top-k for decode and for prefill chunks whose longest row reaches 32K tokens, through the adapters #52882 added for DeepSeek-V4. Related: #55327, #50470, #46172, #60012.

## Claims

- GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, `--max-model-len 133120`: 128K/1K TPOT -7.0% / -4.6% / -3.0% at c1 / c8 / c16, MTP3 c8 -3.0%; 8K/1K within noise; gsm8k and passkey unchanged.
- DeepSeek-V3.2, TP4, default max_model_len (163840): 128K/1K c1 TPOT -15.6%, 4K/1K c16 -1.1%, 4K/1K c1 +0.7% (+0.085 ms); gsm8k unchanged.
- Compressed indexers, other `index_topk`, GLM-5.3-Flash kpool, gfx942, AITER off and non-ROCm are unchanged.

## Validation

- `test_top_k_per_row.py`, MI355X: 43 passed (8 new), 246 skipped, 1 failed as on main (pre-existing, see below). glm5next dispatch tests pass. pre-commit clean.
- AITER vs in-tree on FP8 scorer output: same selections on 29,934 rows (by value where scores tie).
- Serving, mean TPOT (ms), GLM-5.2-MXFP4 unless noted; main 2 runs / PR 3 runs (4 each with MTP3, 2 each for DeepSeek-V3.2), no failed requests:

| workload | main | PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128K/1K c1 / c8 / c16 | 14.73 / 45.05 / 78.94 | 13.70 / 42.97 / 76.60 | -7.0% / -4.6% / -3.0% |
| MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 34.84 | 33.79 | -3.0% |
| 8K/1K c1 / c8 / c16, MTP3 c8 | 13.48 / 17.37 / 22.66 / 9.06 | 13.45 / 17.39 / 22.54 / 9.16 | within noise |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 128K/1K c1 | 16.23 | 13.70 | -15.6% |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c1 / c16 | 12.81 / 22.86 | 12.90 / 22.61 | +0.7% / -1.1% |

- gsm8k 5-shot strict: GLM-5.2 0.9287 main, 0.9348 PR (stderr 0.007); DeepSeek-V3.2 0.9522 main, 0.9507 PR (stderr 0.006). MTP3 acceptance length 3.29 / 3.30.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, kernel data and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source, MI355X.

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, mean TPOT per run (ms). Order: main, PR, PR, main, PR. A further main run between the two PR sessions was dropped: another process held about 88 GiB per GPU while it started, so its KV cache was 1.23M tokens instead of 3.2M. MTP3 order: main, PR, PR, main, PR, PR, main, main.

| workload | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8K/1K c1 | 13.43, 13.53 | 13.44, 13.45, 13.46 |
| 8K/1K c8 | 17.27, 17.47 | 17.27, 17.51, 17.38 |
| 8K/1K c16 | 22.46, 22.86 | 22.44, 22.66, 22.52 |
| 128K/1K c1 | 14.72, 14.75 | 13.66, 13.67, 13.78 |
| 128K/1K c8 | 44.55, 45.56 | 42.95, 42.98, 42.98 |
| 128K/1K c16 | 78.89, 79.00 | 76.58, 76.62, 76.60 |
| MTP3 8K/1K c8 | 8.91, 9.16, 9.08, 9.10 | 9.14, 9.34, 9.08, 9.10 |
| MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 34.27, 35.52, 34.45, 35.12 | 33.96, 33.67, 34.17, 33.35 |

- Median ITL (ms): 128K c1 14.83 to 13.76, c8 18.22 to 17.01, c16 21.52 to 20.49, MTP3 128K c8 27.04 to 25.39. Output throughput at 128K: +5.8% / +3.7% / +2.8%. KV cache size and startup time match across arms.
- The 128K c1 ITL drop (1.07 ms) matches the kernel estimate of 21 indexer layers x 53 us (1.11 ms).
- gsm8k flexible: 0.9295 main, 0.9363 PR. MTP3 gsm8k, first 400 questions: 0.935 main, 0.9325 PR (stderr 0.012). Passkey at 32K / 64K / 120K: 12/12, 8/8, 6/6 in both arms.
- Operator check: decode logits from AITER's `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (buffer poisoned past each row), prefill logits from `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`, calls mirroring `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`; widths 133120 and 1M, `next_n` 1 (1-D), 2 (native 2-D) and 4 (one row per token), packed multi-sequence prefill, and graph replay with new lengths. Every row has `min(L, k)` distinct indices in `[0, L)` followed by `-1`.

DeepSeek-V3.2 (FP8 checkpoint), TP4, same env and flags but no `--max-model-len` (163840), mean TPOT per run (ms), order main, PR, PR, main; median ITL and output throughput follow TPOT:

| workload | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4K/1K c1 | 12.83, 12.80 | 12.91, 12.89 |
| 4K/1K c16 | 22.84, 22.88 | 22.62, 22.60 |
| 128K/1K c1 | 16.24, 16.22 | 13.72, 13.69 |

- 4K/1K c16 mean TTFT: 2333, 2326 ms main, 2465, 2327 ms PR. 128K/1K c1 output throughput +10.0%. KV cache 2.07M tokens in every session. gsm8k flexible: 0.9530 main, 0.9507 PR.
- A static cut-off for 131072-200000 columns would put this deployment back on the in-tree kernel: it would recover the 0.085 ms at 4K c1 and lose the 128K gain (2.53 ms) and the 4K c16 gain. GLM-5.2 at 133120 would lose its 128K gains as well.

Decode top-k per indexer layer (us, in-tree to AITER), GLM-5.2 indexer (32 heads, k=2048); scoring and top-k for 21 layers captured in one graph, LLC flushed before each replay, median of 20:

| width | context | 1 row | 8 rows | 16 rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 133120 | 4K | 17.5 to 20.4 | 17.3 to 22.3 | 17.2 to 22.7 |
| 133120 | 32K | 34.0 to 22.2 | 34.9 to 22.8 | 34.7 to 23.5 |
| 133120 | 128K | 80.8 to 27.9 | 81.8 to 28.8 | 81.3 to 28.5 |
| 1M | 4K | 37.0 to 25.9 | 35.3 to 29.3 | 35.3 to 35.3 |
| 1M | 32K | 42.8 to 26.8 | 42.3 to 29.6 | 43.7 to 32.3 |
| 1M | 128K | 46.3 to 27.1 | 50.0 to 31.2 | 50.2 to 34.4 |

MTP1 (2-D bounds) and MTP3 (one row per token) follow the same pattern. At 262144 columns AITER wins at every measured context.

Prefill top-k GPU time per 16K-row chunk (us, in-tree to AITER): context 16K 304 to 370, 20K 426 to 469, 24K 568 to 558, 32K 757 to 680, 64K 1681 to 1320, 128K 4026 to 2635. 512-row chunks cross over near 20K. Host enqueue per call: in-tree 5-12 us, AITER 27-36 us.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 133120 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
# MTP3: --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# DeepSeek-V3.2: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2, same env and flags without --max-model-len.

# 128K/1K: num-prompts max(C, 3). 8K/1K: --random-input-len 8192,
# num-prompts max(3C, 6), --seed 42. MTP3 c8: 8 prompts at 128K, 24 at 8K.
# DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K: --random-input-len 4096, 6 prompts at c1, 48 at c16, --seed 42.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --seed 43

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py
```

</details>

## Details

- Gate: compress ratio 1 and k=2048 only. Decode always takes AITER (FULL graphs are not keyed by context length); prefill when `chunk.max_seqlen_k`, a host int, reaches 32K.
- Cost: with max_model_len between 131072 and 200000 and up to 48 rows, AITER loses 3-6 us per layer below 8-16K context. DeepSeek-V3.2 (default 163840, 61 indexer layers) measures +0.085 ms TPOT at 4K/1K c1. Keeping the in-tree kernel for that width band would also give up the 2.53 ms gain at 128K on the same deployment, so the gate does not exclude it.
- Not measured end to end: GLM-5/5.1, TP8. CI (MI300, NVIDIA) runs only the new selection test; the GPU tests need gfx950.

<details>
<summary>Design notes, pre-existing failure and related PRs</summary>

- Cause: the in-tree decode kernel has gfx950 policies only for k=512 and k=1024 (#55327). At k=2048 its cost grows with context; AITER's stays near flat.
- Semantics come from #52882's wrappers. ROCm DSA decode carries `(B, next_n)` bounds for native MTP1 and one row per token otherwise, so `seq_lens.reshape(-1)` with `next_n=1` gives AITER each row's exact end. Prefill turns AITER's chunk-global indices into sequence-local ones and keeps `-1`.
- Decode is not split by context length because a FULL graph replays one kernel for every length. Eager decode could use the length, but would then pick a different kernel for the same shape depending on graph mode. AITER's extra host time per call only shows in eager steps.
- `test_aiter_decode_topk_matches_per_row_under_mtp` (from #58167, `requires_gfx950`, so not in CI) fails identically on main: it passes `(B, 1)` seq_lens with `next_n=4` to the in-tree k=512 gfx950 kernel, which reads any 2-D `seq_lens` per row, so its reference rows are wrong. It does not reach the code changed here.
- #60012 (open) tunes the in-tree k=2048 kernel above 200000 columns for #55327. With this PR it still serves AITER-off deployments and short prefill chunks; the gate should be re-measured if it lands. #57844 (open) edits the same selector. #59421 (draft, native MTP above `next_n=2`) is compatible because decode flattens the bounds.
- #50470 (draft) and #46172 also move the k=2048 decode top-k to AITER. Both have merge conflicts and no activity since 2026-08-22, and both swap the call unconditionally, passing vLLM's `next_n` with its 2-D MTP bounds. On both, the author of #52882 noted that AITER v0.1.19 needs those bounds adapted and asked to treat #52882 as the consolidated direction; #52882 then merged with AITER enabled for compressed indexers only. This PR applies its adapters to the k=2048 path, adds prefill and serving results, and leaves every other indexer unchanged. The `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode` entry point that #50470 waited for ships in AITER 0.1.25 and is the function called here.
- Duplicate search, `gh pr list --state all --search`: "aiter topk", "top-k ROCm", "topk ROCm", "indexer ROCm", "indexer aiter", "DeepSeek-V3.2 ROCm", "GLM-5 ROCm", "sparse indexer AMD", "top_k_per_row_decode", "top_k_per_row_prefill", "compress_ratio aiter topk".

</details>

Not a duplicate: #50470 and #46172 target the same decode call, have been inactive since 2026-08-22, and were marked superseded by #52882's author; #52882 left k=2048 on the in-tree kernel (details above). Thanks @JH-Leon-KIM-AMD for #50470.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

- `test_aiter_decode_topk_matches_per_row_under_mtp` (from #58167, `requires_gfx950`, so not in CI) fails identically on main: it passes `(B, 1)` seq_lens with `next_n=4` to the in-tree k=512 gfx950 kernel, which reads any 2-D `seq_lens` per row, so its reference rows are wrong. It does not reach the code changed here.
- #60012 (open) tunes the in-tree k=2048 kernel above 200000 columns for #55327. With this PR it still serves AITER-off deployments and short prefill chunks; the gate should be re-measured if it lands. #57844 (open) edits the same selector. #59421 (draft, native MTP above `next_n=2`) is compatible because decode flattens the bounds.
- #50470 (draft) and #46172 also move the k=2048 decode top-k to AITER. Both have merge conflicts and no activity since 2026-08-22, and both swap the call unconditionally, passing vLLM's `next_n` with its 2-D MTP bounds. On both, the author of #52882 noted that AITER v0.1.19 needs those bounds adapted and asked to treat #52882 as the consolidated direction; #52882 then merged with AITER enabled for compressed indexers only. This PR applies its adapters to the k=2048 path, adds prefill and serving results, and leaves every other indexer unchanged. The `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode` entry point that #50470 waited for ships in AITER 0.1.25 and is the function called here.
- Duplicate search, `gh pr list --state all --search`: "aiter topk", "top-k ROCm", "topk ROCm", "indexer ROCm", "indexer aiter", "DeepSeek-V3.2 ROCm", "GLM-5 ROCm", "sparse indexer AMD", "top_k_per_row_decode", "top_k_per_row_prefill", "compress_ratio aiter topk".

</details>

Not a duplicate: #50470 and #46172 target the same decode call, have been inactive since 2026-08-22, and were marked superseded by #52882's author; #52882 left k=2048 on the in-tree kernel (details above). Thanks @JH-Leon-KIM-AMD for #50470.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

+def _assert_leading_topk(indices: torch.Tensor, row_ends: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    """The sparse-MLA index remap reads only the first min(len, k) slots of a
+    row, so those must hold distinct in-range indices and the rest must be -1."""
+    ends = row_ends.reshape(-1, 1)
+    slots = torch.arange(indices.shape[1], device=indices.device)[None, :]
+    leading = slots < ends.clamp(0, indices.shape[1])
+    assert torch.all(torch.where(leading, (indices >= 0) & (indices < ends), True))
+    assert torch.all(indices[~leading] == -1)
+    ordered = indices.sort(1).values
+    assert not ((ordered[:, 1:] == ordered[:, :-1]) & (ordered[:, 1:] >= 0)).any()
+
+
+def _distinct_logits(rows: int, num_columns: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Distinct values per row: the selected set is unique, so it must match.
+    return torch.rand(rows, num_columns, device="cuda").argsort(dim=1).float()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_columns", [16_384, 133_120, 1_048_576])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("next_n", [1, 2])
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="This test requires ROCm")
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_aiter_dsa_decode_topk_matches_per_row(num_columns: int, next_n: int) -> None:
+    """DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5 decode (uncompressed, k=2048): AITER must select
+    the in-tree kernel's indices, in the leading slots of each row."""
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+
+    top_k = 2048
+    if not rocm_aiter_ops.is_indexer_top_k_enabled():
+        pytest.skip("AITER top-k is unavailable")
+
+    lengths = torch.tensor(
+        [0, 1, 2047, 2048, 2049, 5000, num_columns - 3, num_columns],
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+    offsets = torch.arange(next_n, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    row_ends = (lengths[:, None] - next_n + 1 + offsets).clamp_min(0)
+    seq_lens = row_ends if next_n > 1 else row_ends.flatten()
+    rows = row_ends.numel()
+
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    logits = _distinct_logits(rows, num_columns)
+    columns = torch.arange(num_columns, device="cuda")
+    logits.masked_fill_(columns[None, :] >= row_ends.reshape(-1, 1), 1e20)
+
+    native = torch.full((rows, top_k), -777, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode(
+        logits,
+        next_n,
+        seq_lens,
+        native,
+        rows,
+        logits.stride(0),
+        logits.stride(1),
+        top_k,
+    )
+    aiter = torch.full_like(native, -777)
+    rocm_aiter_ops.indexer_top_k_decode(logits, 1, seq_lens.reshape(-1), aiter, top_k)
+
+    for indices in (native, aiter):
+        _assert_leading_topk(indices, row_ends)
+    assert torch.equal(native.sort(1).values, aiter.sort(1).values)
+
+

+    for indices in (native, aiter):

+    assert torch.equal(native.sort(1).values, aiter.sort(1).values)
